image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

raw_comment: I noticed that 37 states - more than half of all states in the U.S. - are not on track to collect responses from 99% of addresses by September 30 (as indicated by the orange graphs). 13 states, however, are on track (as indicated by the gray graphs). The states that are on track have less than 10% of addresses uncounted for. I also noticed that the graphs of each state are placed based on geographic location. Based on the graph, one can infer that the greatest percentages of people being uncounted for are located in southern states with the exception of Montana. It seems that larger states or more densely populated states have more people that are uncounted. This could be due to the difficulty of counting everyone in a state with such a large population. I wonder why people aren't filling out this census form. Is it accidental or is it on purpose? Is it because they are not educated on the process or its benefits? Do some residents not fill it out due to citizenship status? In those regards, I wonder who are the people being counted for in each state and who are not; it would be interesting to see if certain communities are more or less likely to fill out the census and any characteristics they share. This impacts my community because if not everyone is being counted, then we will not receive all the resources that we need. The census has a large impact when it comes to federal and state funding. A headline for this graph could be The 2020 Census: Who's Really Being Counted.

- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |

| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

Welcome to Wednesday's moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graphs show the projected percentage of addresses not counted by the U.S. Census by state as of September 30, 2020.  You may want to compare these state projections to the most current actual statistics.  They can be found on the U.S. Census “Total Response Rates buy State” website (https://2020census.gov/en/response-rates/nrfu.html).

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?",  "What do you wonder?", and “What impact does this topic have on you and your community?”

Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in the graphs. 

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the article that included these visual representations and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.
Note that you can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

Keep noticing and wondering.  Stay tuned for next week’s graph about consumer spending during the pandemic.

image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that only 13 states are on track to collect almost all of the responses for the 2020 census by September 30. That leaves most of the states – 37 to be exact– without responses from all of their residents. I notice that the states lacking full participation from their residents are highlighted in orange, while the states who received enough responses are depicted in grey. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder how significantly the lack of responses will affect the validity of the 2020 census. I wonder if the states who are lacking responses are doing anything to motivate their citizens to complete the census.

What impact does this have on you and your community?
As a resident of New Jersey, this information impacts my community because the state of New Jersey is highlighted in orange, meaning that it is not on track to receive responses from 99% of its population. Additionally, New Jersey is densely populated which most likely creates a more significant impact on the census data. The data collected from the census will determine whether or not the state government needs to improve roads or create more housing. Therefore, it is imperative that the data is accurate so my community can be served in the best way possible.

image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
Faceted **small-multiple area/line charts** (one mini chart per state), with a solid line/filled area for observed values and a dashed line for projected values.

**2. Layout techniques**  
- **Faceting / small multiples** by **state**  
- No stacking  
- Each facet uses the same axes/scales for comparison  
- Color is used to distinguish state status categories (orange vs. gray)

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| State | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate small panels; state name as panel label |
| Date | Temporal | Position on x-axis within each panel; vertical reference/end-date markers shown in example panel |
| Share of uncounted addresses | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; filled area height; line position |
| Projection status (observed vs. projected) | Categorical/nominal | Line style (solid vs. dashed); shaded/forecast continuation visually separated |
| On-track status / state grouping | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of series and fill (orange vs. gray) |
| Example projected Sept. 30 value for Georgia (“4%”) | Quantitative | Text annotation and highlighted point marker |
